raw_arguments.summary: Outbox delivery throughput (~2.2/s) is below the arrival rate (3.2/s), so a backlog grows (12 to 912, oldest 410 s). Deliveries succeed but are slow; the single serial poller looks like the bottleneck.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog grows because the publish rate is below the commit rate: 2.2/s vs 3.2/s, 900 undelivered over the window.
findings.reason: Pending 12->912 and oldest undelivered age 0.8s->410s match the late-notification symptom.

findings.claim: No delivery failures: all 1980 attempts succeeded with zero auth, network or server errors, and the transfers API was healthy.
findings.reason: Failed gauge is 0 and outcome counts are all success; requests all 201 with p95 0.24s. Failure/retry is not the cause.

findings.claim: Throughput is capped by one poller doing serial ~452ms deliveries (~2.2/s), dominated by consumer handler time (~401ms), below the 3.2/s arrivals.
findings.reason: 1/0.452s is ~2.2/s, equal to the observed publication rate; config shows a single poller. Serial processing within a batch is not directly observed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer auth or network problems slow delivery or cause retries.
alternatives.reason: Zero errors, consumer_auth_ms p50 only 51ms, unattributed time ~1.2ms.

alternatives.hypothesis: Upstream transfer API slowness or errors delay creation of outbox rows.
alternatives.reason: All requests were 201 with p95 0.24s, and arrivals (3.2/s) match request rate (3.21/s).

limitations: Consumer is a fixture (E4), so the ~401ms handler time may not reflect production.
Poller concurrency and batch execution (serial vs parallel) were not directly observed; the bottleneck is inferred from rates.
next_checks: Check how the poller processes a batch (serial vs concurrent) and per-cycle batch sizes and durations.
Test with more pollers or concurrent delivery, or a faster consumer handler, and see if the backlog drains.

findings.claim: Per-delivery latency of about 450 ms, mostly consumer handler time, together with one sequential poller, likely caps throughput near 2.2/s.

raw_arguments.summary: Outbox backlog grew because arrivals (3.2/s) exceeded publication throughput (2.2/s), which is limited by one poller, batch size 20 and a roughly 450 ms per-attempt delivery time.

findings.claim: Outbox publications lag arrivals: 900 more arrivals than publications; pending grew 12 to 912; oldest undelivered age 0.8 s to 410 s.
findings.reason: Tool-computed counts show a growing backlog with zero failures, matching minutes-late notifications.

findings.claim: Deliveries are not failing or erroring: all 1980 succeeded, with no auth, network or server errors, and the transfers route returned only 201s.
findings.reason: Zero non-success outcomes and zero server errors rule out failures and retries as the source of delay.

findings.claim: Publish capacity is bounded by the single poller's config and per-attempt latency (~452 ms, mostly consumer handler time), below the 3.2/s arrival rate.
findings.reason: One poller with batch 20 and 1 s poll gives a roughly 2.2/s observed rate; attempts take ~450 ms with ~401 ms in the consumer handler. The sequential-delivery mechanism is not directly shown.

alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer auth or handler slowness is the root cause
alternatives.reason: Handler time (~401 ms) is stable (p95 405) and every delivery is well under the 3000 ms timeout; it contributes to per-attempt time but is not erratic.

alternatives.hypothesis: Delivery failures or retries cause the delay
alternatives.reason: Zero failed deliveries and zero error outcomes were observed.

limitations: The window is only 15 minutes, with a fixture consumer, so production consumer latency may differ.
Poller internals (sequential vs concurrent delivery within a batch) were not observed directly.
next_checks: Check whether the poller delivers a batch sequentially and whether the poll loop's cycle time is about 0.9 s.
